title: Contract stitcher & gap handler for OpenAI-style tools and legacy function surfaces
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a lightweight stitching layer that reconciles OpenAI-style tool calls with our legacy function invocation surface to preserve backwards compatibility while enabling new structured outputs and streaming semantics.
background: Customers and internal SDKs use a mix of OpenAI-style 'tools' (name + JSON schema) and older 'functions' (positional/typed params). Discrepancies in naming, parameter shapes, and streaming invocation behavior cause runtime errors and increased customer support. Previous attempts (adapters/shims) solved narrow cases but created brittle mappings and runtime forks.
proposal_summary: Create a 'contract stitcher' component in the request router that: 1) canonicalizes tool/function names via a configurable alias table and fuzzy matcher; 2) synthesizes missing parameter envelopes using schema-driven transformers; 3) preserves invocation provenance (original surface, matched target, score); 4) supports streaming passthrough for chunked tool outputs; and 5) emits telemetry and a suggested backfill for ambiguous mappings.
technical_notes:
- Alias resolution: use a ranked matcher (exact > case-insensitive > levenshtein threshold > context-hint) with confidence score.
- Signature reconciliation: prefer JSON-schema-driven coercion and key remapping rules; fall back to positional-binding adapter when schema absent.
- Streaming: maintain a thin framing layer so token streams from model to tool preserve boundary markers; enable early-exit fallback to legacy sync invocation if tool can't accept streamed input.
- Performance: keep avg added latency < 3ms for warm mappings via in-memory cache; cold alias misses trigger async mapping suggestion job.
- Observability: emit events for mapping decisions, failures, coercions, and fallbacks (trace ID tagged).
design_considerations: Tradeoffs: heavier reconciliation logic increases surface area for bugs but reduces customer-facing errors. We avoid heavyweight semantic parsing in the hot path by: 1) caching mapping results, 2) doing expensive fuzzy-match learning offline, and 3) providing a metrics-driven opt-out for strict mode. Must consider RBAC and audit trails when canonicalizing names across customer namespaces.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: API surface spec and unit tests (this ticket) - implement canonicalizer and simple schema transformer behind a feature flag.
Phase 2: Integration - wire streaming passthrough and provenance telemetry; run e2e matrix against representative legacy functions and OpenAI-style tool manifests.
Phase 3: Canary - enable for 5% of requests with automatic rollback on error-rate regression; monitor mapping confidence and customer errors.
Phase 4: Full rollout and backfill - supply suggested mappings to customers via Console; provide migration guide and 'strict' opt-in.
Phase 5: Post-rollout - run a 30-day analysis to convert high-confidence suggestions into default aliases and remove legacy special-casing.
acceptance_criteria: Canonicalizer correctly maps 95% of known aliases in the test corpus without manual overrides.
Average added latency for mapped calls < 3ms for 99th percentile on staging.
Streaming passthrough preserves message boundaries and works end-to-end with example streaming tools (chat-completion -> streaming-csv-writer).
Telemetry emitted for every mapping decision and flagged ambiguous mappings appear in the Console suggestions panel.
Backward-compat tests (legacy functions) pass across the E2E matrix including positional and typed parameter shapes.
test_plan: Unit tests for matcher ranking and threshold behavior.
Property tests for schema coercion (string->int, missing optional keys, nested objects).
Synthetic load tests to verify latency and cache hit behavior.
E2E tests that exercise streaming tool invocations, ensuring chunk ordering and early-close semantics.
User-level regression tests that replay historical call traces to detect changed semantics.
